inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 consolidated cash flow statement share-based compensation add-back (CAD 6M); EquityAwardTaxes nil (Metrics.csv). SBC is immaterial (0.1% of revenue) -- kept explicit, not deleted.
inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted: Q2 FY2026 weighted-average dilutive shares 113,546,523 (Class I 100,985,167 + Class II 11,542,320 basic at 2026-06-30 plus treasury-stock dilution of 2,862,341 options). Held FLAT: SBC is expensed in the flows; NCIB (513,500 shares, CAD 26M in FY2025) merely funds the flat count. Post the Dec-2025 ATCO Arrangement, Sentgraf is the sole Class II holder.
inputs.net_debt_basis: Q2 FY2026 balance sheet: long-term debt 12,751 non-current + 34 current + bank indebtedness 15 = 12,800 total debt; cash 625. Excludes IFRS 16 lease liabilities (192, in equity_bridge) and CU/CU Inc. equity preferred shares (1,709, equity-classified, deducted inside the NCI bridge item).
inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in CAD, the currency of the flows. Risk-free: Government of Canada 10-year 3.93% (Bank of Canada Valet BD.CDN.10YR.DQ.YLD, 2026-10-08). ERP 5.0%, levered equity beta ~0.55 for a regulated-utility holdco -> cost of equity ~6.7%. Pre-tax cost of debt ~5.0% (CU Inc. 4.79% / CU subordinated notes 5.45% issued Sep-2025) -> ~3.9% after 23% tax. Market weights: equity 17.1B (ATCO market cap 9.0B + CU minority 6.4B + preferreds 1.7B) vs debt 12.4B = 58/42 -> WACC 5.5%. Used in ALL scenarios (risk charged once, in the flows and weights). Sensitivity is extreme because equity is a ~30% slice of consolidated EV: each 25bp on WACC moves base value ~CAD 20/share; the current price clears at roughly 5.25%.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (A), leases as debt: IFRS 16 lease liabilities (27 current + 165 non-current = 192 at 2026-06-30) deducted once in equity_bridge; lease principal (TTM ~37M) NOT deducted from the flows; post-IFRS-16 EBITDA used throughout, so EV and EBITDA are lease-consistent.
inputs.nci_treatment: Flows are fully consolidated (100% of Canadian Utilities), so the 47.6% CU minority is deducted ONCE, in the bridge, at MARKET value: 0.476 x 272.33M CU shares (stockanalysis.com, 2026-10-09) = 129.6M shares x CU.TO 49.23 (2026-10-09 close) = 6,381M, plus CU Ltd/CU Inc. equity preferred shares held by NCI at book net of issue costs 1,709M (FY2025 note 28). Book NCI is 3,922M; market is the correct claim because CU is listed and, under the Emera deal, the minority's claim is literally crystallising at 0.755 EMA shares per CU share (CU 49.23 = 0.755 x EMA 65.20 to the cent). Used uniformly across scenarios (engine constraint): in a deal-breaks world the minority claim would fall with CU's price, so the bear is overstated to the downside by roughly CAD 8-10/share. Alternative proportional treatment (NCI = 47.6% of CU's share of DCF equity) would add ~CAD 10/share to base. Neltume Ports (40%, equity-accounted, ~31M/yr associate earnings) is left inside EBITDA and NOT added to the bridge -- matching-asset rule, income in flows so no asset added; immaterial (1.3% of EBITDA). Adelaide Wind 25% NCI and Espaciomovil NCI are immaterial and ignored.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF on the CONSOLIDATED entity (CU 100% + wholly-owned Structures & Logistics, Investments) with the CU minority deducted at market in the bridge -- the engine route the orchestrator requested, adapted per owner-fcf-adaptations (b) leases, (c) NCI, (f) risk-once. The SKILL.md routing table also points at 'Live takeover -> deal-completes vs deal-breaks weighting' and 'holdco -> sum of parts'; both are honoured INSIDE the three-scenario frame: bull = Emera deal completes (combined-entity 7-8% rate-base growth, exit at a sector multiple), base = standalone fair value at house WACC while the deal is pending, bear = deal breaks plus Alberta regulatory downside, and the weights are a deal-probability judgment. The deal-implied value is reported as a cross-check in valuation_philosophy, not as the model. BASIS: shareholders' equity and net income in core_metrics are ATTRIBUTABLE (ex-NCI); the DCF deliberately uses the CONSOLIDATED flows (revenue, EBITDA, D&A, capex, cash tax -- all consolidated by construction) and kpis.NetIncomeInclNCI/TotalEquityInclNCI for the calibration, then removes the minority once in the bridge. BASE YEAR: TTM to 2026-06-30, NOT FY2025 GAAP -- FY2025 net income (150M) was depressed by 572M pre-tax / 253M after-tax-and-NCI impairments charged to the 'depreciation, amortization and impairments' line; EBITDA is unaffected (2,273 FY2025; 2,376 TTM) and D&A is taken EX-impairment (FY2025 1,413 - 572 = 841; TTM 866 = 16.3% of revenue). Adjusted earnings grew 481 -> 518 (FY2024->FY2025) and 261 -> 279 (H1 2025 -> H1 2026). last_fcf (779) is reported OCF less capex less SBC on the IFRS presentation, i.e. AFTER ~500M of interest paid; it is a memo anchor only -- the projections are an unlevered component build and net debt is deducted once in the bridge. Interest income (TTM ~69M) is NOT stripped: the company is net-debt 12.2B, no cash pile to double count. Working-capital capture 0: regulated revenue has deferral accounts and the Structures book roughly nets. Price is a regular TSX close, not after-hours. DEAL TERMS: the Emera announcement (2026-10-06) post-dates every extracted filing; the CU-side ratio (0.755 EMA per non-ATCO CU Class A) is corroborated by the CU print; the ATCO-specific ratio was not obtainable from the filings and the deal-implied ATCO value below uses the 0.755 ratio on ATCO's 142.7M CU shares as a proxy.

equity_bridge.item: NCI: 47.6% of Canadian Utilities common at market (129.6M CU shares x CU.TO 49.23, 2026-10-09)
equity_bridge.note: FY2025 note 28 ownership 47.6%; CU shares 272.33M (stockanalysis.com). Deal-parity price: 0.755 x EMA.TO 65.20.

equity_bridge.item: NCI: CU Ltd / CU Inc. equity preferred shares held by minorities (book net of issue costs)
equity_bridge.note: FY2025 note 28: CU Inc. 190 + CU Ltd 1,552 - 33 issuance costs. Perpetual rate-reset prefs, market ~par. Q2 FY2026 MD&A mentions a further $200M pref issuance to pre-fund growth; not yet on the 2026-06-30 balance sheet.

equity_bridge.item: IFRS 16 lease liabilities (treatment A, leases as debt)
equity_bridge.note: Q2 FY2026 balance sheet: 27 current + 165 non-current.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: revenue_5yr_cagr (5.5%, FY2020-FY2025) tempered to the rate-base-driven run-rate; equity and EPS CAGRs are distorted (see notes)
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Attributable equity CAGR (1.1% 3yr / 2.2% 5yr) diverges >30% from revenue 5yr CAGR (5.5%): FY2025 equity was cut by 253M of after-tax-and-NCI impairments and ATCO pays out ~45% of adjusted earnings plus NCIB. GAAP EPS CAGRs (-25.6% 3yr, -9.5% 5yr) are the FY2025 impairment trough (EPS 1.34 vs adjusted 4.61); the adjusted-EPS series grew 3.82 -> 4.29 -> 4.61 (FY2023-FY2025, +9.9%/yr). Use the adjusted series.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF series = reported FCF - SBC (SBC 1-8M/yr, immaterial; interest income not stripped, net-debt company): FY2020 814, FY2021 516, FY2022 810, FY2023 396, FY2024 385, FY2025 638. The decline is the capex supercycle (capex 1,028 -> 1,840 FY2020-FY2025, Yellowhead/CETO/rental fleet) on the IFRS post-interest OCF presentation, not an earnings decline: consolidated EBITDA grew 1,739 -> 2,273 (5.5%/yr). FCF CAGRs are therefore not a growth proxy for this business and were not used to select the growth rate.

base.narrative: Standalone ATCO while the Emera transaction is pending. Revenue compounds at ~5% near term (Alberta rate base +6-7%, Yellowhead CAD 2.9B in service ~2027-28, AA6 ROE step-up in Australia, Structures & Logistics high-single-digit) fading to 2.5% inflation-indexed. EBITDA margin drifts 44.5% -> 45.0% (TTM 44.7%). Capex stays at 35% of revenue through the Yellowhead build then tapers to 25% (1.5x D&A, the reinvestment a 2.5%-growing rate base needs on ~3.8x PP&E/revenue). Cash tax ramps 5% -> 20% as CCA deferrals unwind (TTM cash rate 2.6%, book 21-23%). Terminal: Gordon at 5.5%/2.5% (34.2x FCF, ~10.4x year-10 EBITDA, a derating from 12.4x today) binds below the 36x cap -- no multiple expansion assumed.

bull.narrative: Deal completes (target close Q3/Q4 2027): the utility assets ride the combined Emera/CU CAD 32B capital plan at 7-8% rate-base growth, Alberta's market redesign settles by 2028 and EnPower curtailment eases, AA6 lifts Australian returns, Structures & Logistics compounds on housing and defence demand, and the larger balance sheet keeps cash taxes deferred longer (terminal 17%). Margins reach 46%. Terminal growth held at 2.5% and WACC at 5.5% (risk charged once); Gordon (34.2x) binds below the 37x cap. Cross-check: lands within a few dollars of the deal consideration at the announcement-date EMA price (see valuation_philosophy).

bear.narrative: Deal breaks (regulatory objection -- AUC public-interest review, CFIUS/FIRB -- or Emera's own derating kills the exchange math) AND Alberta turns hostile: PBR2 refund appeal lost and further ROE pressure, EnPower renewables curtailment worsens under the AESO redesign (more impairments), hydrogen assets stranded, Structures & Logistics hits a resource-capex downcycle. Growth fades to 2%, margins compress to 42.5%, cash taxes normalise fast to 23%, growth capex is cut (terminal 24%). Terminal at the 34x cap (~9.4x year-10 EBITDA, a sector-trough multiple). The near-zero result is the leverage: ~CAD 20.5B of fixed and minority claims against a consolidated EV in the low 20s of billions leaves ATCO's equity as a thin residual.

scenario_narratives.base: Standalone fair value at the house 5.5% CAD WACC while the Emera deal is pending: rate-base-driven ~5% growth fading to inflation, margins ~45%, capex supercycle tapering after Yellowhead, cash tax normalising over a decade, terminal at a ~10.4x EBITDA Gordon value. The consolidated EV comes out ~10% below today's market EV (12.4x TTM EBITDA) and, because ATCO's equity is only ~30% of consolidated EV, that gap compounds into a per-share value well below the price.
scenario_narratives.bull: Emera transaction completes on roughly the announced terms (all-share, Sentgraf support, close Q3/Q4 2027) and ATCO holders end up with Emera paper on a 7-8% rate-base grower plus a listed New ATCO (Structures & Logistics, Neltume, retail energy, land). Operating paths follow the combined-entity capital plan; the resulting value coincides with the deal consideration at the announcement-date Emera price.
scenario_narratives.bear: Deal fails and Alberta regulatory/market-design risk compounds: lower allowed returns, more EnPower impairments, cyclical Structures downturn, derating to a sector-trough multiple. Equity is nearly wiped as a residual of ~CAD 20.5B of senior and minority claims -- and that is with the CU minority still deducted at today's deal-parity price, so the bear is if anything too harsh by ~CAD 8-10/share.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: A live, signed, controlling-shareholder-supported transaction breaks the default 15/50/35 frame; the weights are a deal-completes vs deal-breaks judgment. Bull (deal completes) 50%: the scheme has Sentgraf's voting support and both boards, but needs AUC, FERC, CFIUS, HSR, Competition Act, Australian FIRB, courts and three securityholder votes with a 12-15 month runway, and the consideration is Emera stock already at its 52-week low -- so a ~65% completion probability is haircut to 50% for consideration-value risk. Base (standalone, deal pending or renegotiated) 35%. Bear (deal breaks AND Alberta headwinds) 15%: both legs have to happen; a clean deal break alone lands between bear and base.
probability_weighted.band_note: House/street band is degenerate: SBC is 0.1% of revenue, so street IV exceeds house IV by ~CAD 2/share and band_position (hundreds of percent) carries no information. Read it as n/a -- the valuation does not depend on SBC treatment.

entry_price.method: House default: 15% IRR over the 10-year horizon with the terminal value rebuilt at the hurdle, all three scenarios then probability-weighted. No lower-cost exit buyer is baked in: the Emera consideration is stock, not cash, and sits in the bull scenario, not the entry price.

valuation_philosophy.summary: ATCO is a leveraged, consolidated claim on a regulated-utility rate base: consolidated EV ~CAD 29.5B at the market price (12.4x TTM EBITDA) against CAD 12.2B net debt, CAD 1.7B preferreds and a CAD 6.4B CU minority, leaving ATCO's equity a ~30% residual slice. That is why the valuation is a knife-edge on the discount rate (each 25bp of WACC ~CAD 20/share) and why the bear case lands near zero. The house DCF at a CAPM-derived 5.5% CAD WACC values the standalone business below the price; the price itself clears at roughly 5.25% -- i.e. the market is paying the Emera deal, not the standalone. DEAL-IMPLIED CROSS-CHECK (proxy, see inputs.notes): ATCO's 142.7M CU shares x 0.755 EMA shares x EMA 65.20 = CAD 7.0B = CAD 62/ATCO share, plus New ATCO (Structures & Logistics ~CAD 125M adjusted earnings run-rate + Investments ~CAD 45M, ~CAD 170M at 12x = CAD 2.0B = CAD 18/share) = ~CAD 80/share today, ~CAD 86 at the announcement-date EMA price of ~70 -- which is where the bull scenario lands and where the stock trades. Pre-announcement ATCO traded ~CAD 71 (+12.7% on the news). The house 15% hurdle cannot be met from a bond-like asset priced at a ~5.2% implied return; the weighted entry price is far below the market and that is the finding, not a defect. FY2025 GAAP earnings (EPS 1.34) are an impairment trough; the business is valued on consolidated EBITDA/TTM flows and the adjusted-earnings series (4.61 FY2025, 2.48 H1 2026).
key_risks_to_valuation: Discount-rate sensitivity: equity is ~30% of consolidated EV; +/-25bp WACC ~ -/+CAD 20/share in base. GoC 10-year moved to 3.93%; a further 50bp rise takes base value toward zero.
Deal completion and consideration risk: all-share, Emera at a 52-week low, 12-15 month multi-jurisdiction approval path; the bull case is Emera paper plus an untested New ATCO.

NCI valuation basis: CU minority deducted at today's deal-parity price (CAD 6.4B); on a deal break the claim would fall ~CAD 1B (~CAD 9/share of upside to bear/base). A proportional-NCI treatment would add ~CAD 10/share to base.
Alberta regulation: PBR2 refund appeal, 2027+ ROE/PBR resets, AESO market restructuring and transmission constraints (the 2025 EnPower impairment) -- the majority of EBITDA is Alberta-regulated.
Capex supercycle execution: Yellowhead CAD 2.9B and CETO on time/on budget; capex above 35% of revenue for longer than modelled compresses interim FCF, though regulated recovery limits value impact.
Cash tax normalisation pace: a faster unwind of CCA deferrals (bear 23% by year 8) versus a prolonged growth-capex shelter (bull 17%) is worth roughly CAD 10/share.
Terminal-value share: ~80% of EV sits in the terminal in every scenario, as for any regulated utility; the cap multiple only binds in the bear.
valuation_philosophy.sanity_check_note: scripts/sanity_check.py tripped on implied P/E (weighted IV / FY2025 SBC-adjusted GAAP EPS 1.34 = ~49x vs a 19.4x 10-year average). This is a denominator artifact, not a model error: FY2025 GAAP EPS is the impairment trough (572M pre-tax / 253M after-tax-and-NCI write-downs charged to D&A). On FY2025 adjusted EPS of 4.61 (the series management and this valuation use) the implied P/E is 14.8x weighted / 13.7x base, inside the 10.2-19.4x historical range; on H1-2026-annualised adjusted EPS (~4.96) it is ~13.7x / 12.7x. The checker's 'wacc_too_low' candidate was rejected: the 5.5% WACC is CAPM-built on the 3.93% GoC 10-year and risk is already charged once in the flows and deal-probability weights; stacking a regulatory premium would charge Alberta risk twice and drive a regulated-utility equity that is a 30% residual of consolidated EV toward zero. Growth is already at the through-cycle revenue CAGR (5.5% FY2020-25). The checker's historical EV/EBITDA (6.6-8.1x) excludes the CAD 6.4B CU minority from EV and so is not comparable to the consolidated 12.4x the market pays today or the ~10.4x year-10 terminal in base. No driver was changed in the fix pass; the trip is documented here and in sanity_check.fix_applied.
